It provided resources, livelihoods, and a basis for obligations/control. This is an assessment background note written for this packet, not an actual historical primary-source quotation.

items.prompt: Name one kind of source that could help check the background note and explain why.
items.answer: A relevant map, scholarly/educator text, community source, historical document, or data record; source must match the claim. One point for suitable source and one for purpose.

items.prompt: Compare a lord’s and a peasant’s roles on a manor.
items.answer: Rubric (3): accurate relevant content (1); supported comparison/relationship (1); clear organization and source/evidence awareness (1). Work, rights/obligations, unequal power, and recognition of regional variation.

practice.title: Computer Science
practice.passage: Tables organize records and attributes. Spreadsheet formulas depend on correct inputs and rules. Label units and check calculated results by another method.

items.prompt: Why check a spreadsheet formula?
items.answer: An incorrect formula can create plausible-looking wrong results.

items.prompt: Enter fictional plant data and calculate a total or average; verify it by hand. Use precise vocabulary, two supporting reasons or observations, and a limitation.
items.answer: Look for a relevant completed activity, an accurate concept, evidence or an example, and a reasoned explanation/revision. Accept varied justified responses. Do not grade beliefs or private experiences.

practice.title: Life Skills
practice.passage: First aid begins with recognizing danger and obtaining appropriate help. Do not enter unsafe scenes. Learn response procedures from current qualified instruction with an adult; classroom practice is not certification.

items.prompt: What precedes helping at an unsafe scene?
items.answer: Protect yourself from danger and seek appropriate adult/emergency help.

items.prompt: Locate supplies and emergency contacts; role-play a fictional help request without placing a real emergency call. Use precise vocabulary, two supporting reasons or observations, and a limitation.
items.answer: Look for a relevant completed activity, an accurate concept, evidence or an example, and a reasoned explanation/revision. Accept varied justified responses. Do not grade beliefs or private experiences.
